provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft; host source restrictions and execution verification

draft_notes.explanation: The factory works out where the original 'down' vector (1,0) and 'right' vector (0,1) end up under the D4 transform. A row reversal negates dx, and each clockwise rotation maps (dy,dx) to (dx,-dy). The palette is applied to the colour roles: the divider is palette[4], the marker palette[5], the background palette[0], and each glyph colour palette[1/2/3/6] gets its own move (right 3, left 2, left 4, down 2). The emitted program finds the divider as the full row or column of the divider colour; whether it looks for a row or a column depends on the transformed down vector. It slices out the canvas on the side the visible R vector points to, and treats the opposite side as the glyph panel. Glyphs are found as 8-connected components and sorted by their minimum projection onto R (which glyph column) and then onto D (position within that column). This reproduces the original order: left column top to bottom, then right column. Starting at the marker, it draws the staircase directly in visible coordinates. A down glyph paints 2 cells along D. A horizontal glyph steps one cell along D and then paints L cells along ±R, reusing the corner cell, and the end cell becomes the new position. Cells outside the canvas are clipped, as in the generator. No grid is rotated or recoloured as a whole.
draft_notes.limitations: This assumes palette is a permutation indexable by the original colours 0..9 and that the generator's layout holds: one full divider line, glyphs only on the far side of it, and one marker. Glyphs whose colour is not a mapped glyph colour are ignored. The fixtures match a single uniform rule; no contradictions were found. Nothing has been executed by me.
